articleTitle: "DYNAMIC DRAWINGS: NEW DEVELOPMENTS IN COMPUTER ASSISTED CARTOON ANIMATION"
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Motion Reproduction in Television
IEE Colloquium on Motion Reproduction in Television
abstract: Previously, the quality of motion reproduction in television has not been an issue. In the drive towards higher definition, the 'definition' is assumed to be spatial, not temporal. There was no requirement for better motion, that is, unless it was in the context of slow-motion replay, which effectively put motion under the microscope, and is the equivalent of high definition. However, the fact that most coding strategies are affected heavily by motion means that there is a need to understand a lot more about it. Little research has gone into the basics of motion perception, as opposed to the perception of impairments to it caused by compression. The author attempts to lay the groundwork of some theory on this matter. The topics of sampling, the film process and TV systems are discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Problems of estimation and measurement of motion in television
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Motion Reproduction in Television
abstract: This paper describes the need for motion estimation and its use in motion compensated interpolation. In particular it describes the many occasions that real television signals fail to follow the rules of the simple motion models used in analysing and developing early motion estimation systems. It reaches the conclusion that a key element of any real time motion estimation system for television signals, is the capability of the motion estimator to monitor its own performance and produce a relevant control signal for the application using the motion vectors.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

abstract: Describes the production of a commercial that is not wholly ' natural' but wavers on the fence between realism and then using the technology to create an obvious special effect. In some areas it also demonstrates the limitations of the technology at the time it was made. The first problem with this commercial was to find archive shots of different famous footballers who have played for Manchester United over the years, and edit them into a logical game sequence.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

abstract: Discusses the concept of virtual TV studio production. Virtual production is the combination of real and synthetic images. Demonstrations of virtual studio production have already been carried out; the operations involved are described.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Interactive motion control and computer graphics
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Motion Reproduction in Television
abstract: Cell Animation is a film and video production and post production house that has been running for 20 years and has developed expertise in motion control, special effects editing and computer graphics. Motion control is the control of film cameras, especially their spatial motion with the use of robotics and computers. The computer control and repeatability of the motion control camera has given it several advantages over normal camera rigs or dollies. Repeat passes are possible that will exactly align. One main achievement at Cell has been the development of a system to be able to take moves from a computer animation and input these into the motion control rig. It is possible to design a whole camera move in the computer, change and edit it and then supply that move to the rig. There are a lot of physical limitations to what the rigs can do but these can be accounted for within the computer animation stage. The method relies in inverse kinematics. Cell has produced several special effects commercials using this technology. The production of these commercials are discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Motion adaption-the everyday solution to varispeed disk playback
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Motion Reproduction in Television
abstract: The paper discusses the implementation of a varispeed playback system for digital disk recorders used as post production image stores and computer graphics image storage devices. The digital disk recorder is almost tailor made for varispeed play, it has huge bandwidth allowing random access to any frame of video, therefore the problem of selecting a pre-set number of frames from contiguous video streams, a constant problem for tape machines, is almost non-existent.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
